2607.21000.title: Naju: A Native Discrete State-Space Model with Independent Retention and Writing for Long-Sequence Memory
2607.21000.paper_summary: Long-sequence memory tracking places two opposing demands on a recurrent state: near-lossless retention of stored bindings over long horizons, and active overwriting of stale ones. In our diagnostic suite, the strongest efficient baselines tend to solve only one side well. Continuous-time-parameterized state-space models (SSMs) such as Mamba obtain their discrete recurrence by zero-order-hold discretization of a continuous-time system; we argue that this detour is unnecessary for memory tracking and parameterize the discrete transition directly. Naju (Native Adaptive Junction Unit) factorizes the recurrent update, schematically $x_n = f_n\odot x_{n-1} + i_n\odot(B_n u_n)$, into an explicit discrete pole (a learned forget gate $f_n$), an independent write gain $i_n$, and input-dependent write/read maps. Since the sigmoid pole satisfies $0<f_n<1$, each frozen local coordinate is Schur-stable by construction, and the full time-varying recurrence satisfies a fading-memory/BIBO bound under uniform boundedness assumptions, with no stability regularizer. We formalize the key structural limitation of coupled designs: any non-expansive complementary single-gate recurrence ties the effective retention $r$ and write gain $w$ through $|r|+w\le 1$, so near-complete retention forces weak writing; decoupling $f_n$ from $i_n$ removes this constraint. Empirically, Naju is the only evaluated model that remains strong on both retention and overwriting at 4x the training length. Beyond the diagnostic suite, we evaluate Naju on WikiText-103 language modeling, Long Range Arena, and multi-query associative recall. Across these settings, Naju consistently combines strong long-range memory with competitive or superior performance, outperforming the Mamba baselines in the principal comparisons while remaining competitive with the Transformer and preserving linear-time, linear-memory scaling.
2607.21000.paper_summary_zh: 長序列記憶追蹤對重複狀態提出了兩個對立的需求：在長時間範圍內幾乎無損地保留存儲的綁定，以及主動覆蓋過時的綁定。在我們的診斷套件中，最強的有效基準往往只能很好地解決其中一個方面。連續時間參數化狀態空間模型（SSMs）如Mamba通過對連續時間系統進行零階保持離散化來獲得其離散重複；我們認為這一繞行對於記憶追蹤來說是多餘的，並直接對離散轉換進行參數化。Naju（原生自適應接合單元）將重複更新分解為一個顯式的離散極點（學習的遺忘閘$f_n$）、一個獨立的寫入增益$i_n$，以及依賴於輸入的寫入/讀取映射。由於sigmoid極點滿足$0<f_n<1$，每個凍結的局部坐標在構造上都是Schur穩定的，並且完整的時間變化重複在均勻有界假設下滿足衰退記憶/BIBO界限，沒有穩定性正則化器。我們形式化了耦合設計的關鍵結構限制：任何非擴展的互補單閘重複通過$|r|+w\le 1$將有效保留$r$和寫入增益$w$聯繫在一起，因此幾乎完全的保留會迫使寫入變弱；將$f_n$與$i_n$解耦可以消除這一限制。在實證上，Naju是唯一在4倍訓練長度下仍在保留和覆寫方面表現強勁的評估模型。除了診斷套件，我們還在WikiText-103語言建模、長距離競技場和多查詢聯想回憶上評估Naju。在這些設置中，Naju始終將強大的長期記憶與具有競爭力或優越的性能相結合，在主要比較中超越Mamba基準，同時與Transformer保持競爭，並保持線性時間、線性記憶的擴展性。
2607.21000.author: Hyuk Lim et.al.
